species.look_here_first: Look where the leaf stalk meets the stem: flowers and long, pointed seed capsules arise there. Check the capsule ribs together with the palmately lobed, toothed leaves.
morphology_keys: Upright herb with stiff hairs on stems and leaves.
Leaves have several palmately arranged lobes and toothed edges.
Flower has a fused stamen column; slender epicalyx bracts sit outside the calyx.
Elongated capsules usually have five ribs and split when mature.
photo_roles: Habit with leaf attachment and fruit positions visible.
Side view of an attached capsule showing its ribs and pointed tip.
Flower side and center showing epicalyx bracts, calyx and stamen column.
species.lookalike_work: Compare with other cultivated Abelmoschus and hibiscus-like mallows; source-backed local comparison remains pending.

species.look_here_first: Turn over a leaflet and inspect its base. Look for blunt teeth bearing raised glands; most of the remaining leaflet edge is smooth. Confirm with the whole compound leaf and, when present, winged fruits.
morphology_keys: Large compound leaves carry numerous leaflets.
Leaflet margins are mostly smooth except for gland-bearing teeth near the base.
Winged fruits have a seed near the middle of the twisted wing.
photo_roles: Complete compound leaf with attachment to twig.
Underside macro of leaflet-base teeth and glands.
Attached fruit cluster and one individual winged fruit.
species.lookalike_work: Black walnut and many sumacs have serrations along much more of the leaflet edge. Inspect margin and basal glands together; retain source-specific comparison rather than a universal claim about every sumac.

species.look_here_first: Examine the large, heart-shaped leaf and its velvety hair covering, then find the branched flower cluster and a mature segmented fruit. Use the fruit and flower structure along with the leaves.
morphology_keys: Shrubby growth with large, soft-haired, heart-shaped leaves.
Five-petaled flowers are borne in branched clusters.
Mature dry fruit separates into seed-bearing segments.
photo_roles: Branch showing leaf attachment and the branched flower cluster.
Both leaf surfaces with hair detail.
Mature fruit and separated segments with a scale.
species.lookalike_work: Exact separating characters against Abutilon and Wissadula require a sourced comparison before adding an identification key.
